core.title: Do not ratify a train-bearing plan whose flow router sanity fails
core.given: A train-bearing plan session at the CONFIRM phase where a required flow router sanity check fails
core.when: The planner attempts to ratify (lock) the plan
core.then: Ratify must refuse to lock the plan, leaving the session unlocked.
prefer: Read the failed rule for the reported user/system flow, flow router and route, fix the plan's flow router, and re-run ratify.
avoid: Marking the session locked/confirmed, even partially, while it is train-bearing and a required flow router sanity check fails.
Making sanity pass by dropping the user/system flow or its routes from the plan instead of fixing the flow router.
core.why: Locking a train-bearing plan whose flow router is unsound would ratify routes that cannot run safely; confirm is the last gate before the plan is fixed.
evidence: The realization's automated check for this rule passes.
On a failing ratify, the plan session remains unlocked and the failure report identifies the session, the user/system flow, the flow router, the route and the failed sanity rule.
verification: Verified as a conditional-requirement check on the ratify (lock) operation of a plan session.
Enforced at the confirm phase: the subject of the check is the plan session, and a failure blocks ratify (confirm-blocking).
A failure report must carry the required failure evidence: session_id, user_system_flow_id, flow_router_id, route_id, failed_rule.

values: plan session carries one or more user/system flows
required flow router sanity check failed

fires: Planner ratifies a train-bearing plan session at CONFIRM, and a required flow router sanity check for one of its routes fails.
At CONFIRM, a ratify attempt on a train-bearing plan session would lock it while a required flow router sanity rule is reported failing.
doesNotFire: Plan session carries no user/system flow (not train-bearing).
All required flow router sanity checks pass at ratify time.
Planning work before the CONFIRM phase that does not attempt to ratify or lock the session.

bunOnly.reason: Names this rule's concrete validator test id in the ATDD-Bun realization; the core keeps only the neutral counterpart (the realization's automated check for this rule passes).

family/template/variant are labels of the ATDD-Bun validation registry and include this rule's variant id; per the not-profile-keys rule the ids stay in the realization and the core's verification describes the same check generically as a conditional requirement.

classification.note: Plan-model wording (train-bearing session, CONFIRM phase, flow router sanity) names no stack; kept verbatim.
Ratify/lock is the planner-model operation, not a stack construct; kept verbatim.
The single obligation (refuse to lock, session stays unlocked) is stack-neutral; kept verbatim.
Rationale is about plan safety, not the stack; kept verbatim.
Remediation path uses only plan-model identifiers (user/system flow, flow router, route, ratify); no concrete example repeated because it is already role-level.
Partial-lock guard is stated at the plan-session level; kept verbatim.
Metric-gaming guard (dropping the user/system flow to evade the gate) is plan-model level; kept verbatim.
Neutral counterpart: the realization's automated check passes. The concrete validator test id is a realization detail (bunOnly).
Unlocked-session outcome and the failure-report field contract are plan-model facts, neutral as prose; the exact field list is also the verification contract in core:verification[2].
The generic shape (conditional requirement on ratify) goes to core:verification[0]; the family/template/variant labels, including this rule's variant id, are ATDD-Bun registry details (bunOnly).
phase=CONFIRM, enforcement=confirm-blocking, subject_kind=plan-session are all plan-model/neutral; mapped to core:verification[1] without the registry key=value notation.
Required failure-evidence fields (session_id, user_system_flow_id, flow_router_id, route_id, failed_rule) are the plan-session model's contract, not stack-specific; mapped to core:verification[2].
Per-rule severity 4 and disposition strict are not profile keys; they belong to the rule's core verification (core:verification[3]).
Phase fact CONFIRM is plan-model neutral; the Bun note's '(validation.phase)' registry reference is dropped (core fact schema carries fact/values/observability only).
Operation values 'ratify'/'lock plan session' are planner-model triggers, observable now.
Finding values (train-bearing session, failed required flow router sanity) are plan-model observations; observability stays needs_new_observer.

neutralityNotes: The whole convention lives in the planner-model domain (plan session, user/system flow, flow router, route, ratify/lock, CONFIRM phase), which is stack-independent by construction: given/when/then/prefer/avoid/why, the activation facts and fires/doesNotFire name no stack, runtime, framework, language, package manager, file suffix or path, so the core keeps them verbatim. The check's subject is a plan session (planner runtime state), not a file location, so the core needs nothing from the structure profile: profileRequirements is empty and no key is proposed. The only realization specifics are this rule's validator/variant ids (evidence[0], verifier_detail[0] labels), classified bunOnly while core:verification describes the check generically. Per-rule severity 4 and strict disposition stay in core:verification per the not-profile-keys rule. The activation facts' notes, which referenced ATDD-Bun validation fields, are not representable in the neutral fact schema and were dropped; their content is otherwise carried by the fact values. 'unless' is empty in bun.json and remains empty in the core (no condition dropped or added).
